name: Multi Location Product & Inventory Management for WooCommerce
author: Plugincy

sections.description:
Multi Location Product & Inventory Management for WooCommerce helps shops that sell from more than one place, including retail branches, warehouses, pickup points, and regional stores. Manage stock for each location from one WooCommerce installation. Shoppers can select a store, browse the products available there, and place orders associated with that location.

Live demo | Documentation

Free Features

Store and warehouse locations

  • Create as many locations as you need and organize them as parent and child locations, for example a city with several branches.
  • Add an address, city, state, postal code, country, email, and phone number for each location. Set the display order and see each location’s city, country, and product count in the Locations list.
  • Assign products to one or more stores. Each store also has a native WooCommerce product archive.

Location-based inventory and Stock Central

  • Manage stock quantities and backorders separately for each location. Each variation of a variable product can have its own stock and backorder setting.
  • Use the Locations column in the WooCommerce product list to check stock by location. The dashboard shows product and location totals and charts for products and stock per location.
  • Use Stock Central to search products and filter by location, category, product type, stock status, or brand. Edit standard WooCommerce stock, product prices, and backorders, along with location assignments, stock, and backorders, from the product editor.
  • Bulk assign products to a store, remove store assignments, or move selected products to the trash. Free uses the normal WooCommerce product price at every location.

Store selection and location-based product availability

  • Add the store selector to a page, widget, or template with [mulopimfwc_store_location_selector]. Use a searchable dropdown, show child locations and product counts, or let shoppers confirm their choice with a button.
  • On product pages, display available locations as a list, buttons, or a dropdown and choose where the selector appears.
  • Remember the shopper’s chosen store in a cookie for a configurable period from 1 to 365 days. You can require store selection before adding products to the cart.
  • Use strict location filtering to show products assigned to the chosen store. You can also include products with no assigned location. Choose whether a product unavailable at the selected store shows an unavailable message or a 404 page.
  • Hide out-of-stock products at the chosen store, display an out-of-stock badge, gray them out, or use the WooCommerce default. Display the chosen store in product titles with your preferred position and separator.
  • Choose whether to show location stock, backorders, or location information, and which user roles see location-specific information.
  • When shoppers switch stores, the cart is checked against the new store’s stock. Items the new store can supply, including allowed backorders, stay in the cart. An optional notice explains changes.

Location orders and fulfillment

  • Save the chosen location with orders placed through classic checkout or WooCommerce Checkout Blocks.
  • View and filter orders by location. Open the order’s Location box to see location information and stock or to change the assigned store.
  • Reduce stock at the order’s location when WooCommerce processes the order and return stock to that location when WooCommerce restocks items. The order tools support High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).

Features in the Separate Pro Plugin

Location-based pricing and checkout rules

  • Set regular and sale prices, purchase costs, and currency per location. View margins by store and apply location-specific coupons and promotions.
  • Configure shipping methods and pickup options, tax classes, and payment gateways by location. Cash on Pickup supports WooCommerce Checkout Blocks when configured.
  • Allow mixed-location carts, group items by store, and split orders by location with compatible settings. Use location-specific fulfillment and transfer cost controls.

Automatic location detection and storefront discovery

  • Use a store selection popup and optional browser or IP location tools to help shoppers find a nearby store. Use a hierarchical selector and display products and availability for the selected location.
  • Build a store locator with OpenStreetMap and Leaflet. Show store contact details, directions, maps, galleries, and business hours. Display Open or Closed status and apply purchase restrictions for closed locations.
  • Show location details on product pages, use product filters and recommendations by location, and configure location-aware product and archive titles, meta descriptions, URLs, and structured data. Pro includes integrations for Yoast SEO and Rank Math.

Location managers, reports, and notifications

  • Assign staff to specific locations and configure permissions for store-level operations. Route supported order emails to the appropriate location managers.
  • Review inventory, orders, revenue, investment, profit, and low stock by location. Export analytics reports and review customer location insights.
  • Configure low-stock and order notifications, email and browser alerts, daily digests, and optional Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Telegram, or webhook notifications.
  • Collect reviews by store, display location-specific ratings, and use optional low-rating notifications. Customize storefront and admin wording with Text Management.

Inventory import, export, and integrations

  • Move settings in JSON and inventory in CSV. Use CSV and ZIP workflows for product and location migration, with validation and background job controls.
  • Connect POS, WMS, or ERP systems through the Pro REST API namespace mulopimfwc/v1 and webhooks. Supported workflows include bulk stock updates, inventory exports, and location and product queries.

View Multi Location Product & Inventory Management Pro

Use Cases

  • Retail chains and franchises can manage products and stock independently at each branch.
  • Multi-warehouse stores can see which warehouse holds each product and associate an order with the right location.
  • Regional stores can show a catalog based on the shopper’s selected store. The separate Pro plugin adds regional prices and currencies.
  • Click and collect stores can use the separate Pro plugin to configure location-specific pickup options and business hours.

Video Tutorial

Third-party libraries

The folder assets/lib holds unchanged minified builds of two open-source libraries. Their readable source code:

  • Chart.js 4.6.2 (MIT), for the dashboard charts.
  • Select2 4.1.0-rc.0 (MIT), for the styled dropdowns.

External services

Plugincy usage reports and optional feedback

Usage reporting is off by default. If you enable Contribute to Plugincy in Settings → Advanced, the plugin sends a report at most once a week to https://plugincy.com/wp-json/product-analytics/v1/track/04. The report includes the site URL, multisite status, WordPress, plugin, PHP and MySQL versions, web server software, timezone region, active theme, active plugin names and versions, and the Free edition identifier. You can turn off usage reporting at any time.

If you select Submit & Deactivate in the optional feedback form, the plugin sends the site URL and the reason you selected or entered to https://plugincy.com/wp-json/product-analytics/v1/deactivate/04. Use Skip & Deactivate to deactivate without submitting the form.

See Plugincy’s Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy.

WordPress.org plugin catalog

When an administrator opens Our Plugins, the page requests Plugincy’s public catalog from the WordPress.org Plugins API. The request includes the author name, requested catalog fields, and standard WordPress connection data. Your browser may also contact WordPress.org to load plugin icons.

See the WordPress.org Plugins API documentation and WordPress.org Privacy Policy.

Support

For support, feature requests or bug reports, please visit Plugincy Support.

Privacy Policy

To learn more about the data we collect and how we use it, please see our Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins → Add New in your WordPress admin and search for Multi Location Product & Inventory Management for WooCommerce.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate. WooCommerce must be active.
  3. Open Location Manage in the admin menu.

Manual installation

  1. Go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, select the ZIP file, and install it.
  2. Activate the plugin and open Location Manage. For an FTP installation, upload the extracted plugin folder into wp-content/plugins/ before activating it.

Getting started

  1. Create locations: go to Location Manage → Locations and add each store with its address and contact details.
  2. Add stock: open a product, tick its stores in the Locations box, then enter the stock at each store in the Location Settings tab. You can also do this in Location Manage → Stock Central.
  3. Add the store selector: place [mulopimfwc_store_location_selector] on a page, in a widget or in your header.
  4. Choose your settings: go to Location Manage → Settings to set filtering, product titles, out-of-stock display and cart behaviour.
  5. Test: choose a store on the shop, add a product to the cart, place an order and check its location and stock.

Store selector shortcode

[mulopimfwc_store_location_selector] shows a dropdown of your stores. Use these attributes to configure it.
  • title – heading text above the dropdown.
  • show_title – on or off.
  • show_button – on to apply the choice with a button instead of at once.
  • use_select2 – on for a searchable dropdown.
  • herichical – on to show child locations under their parent.
  • show_count – on to show the number of products at each store.
  • max_width – width in pixels (default 300).
  • multi_line – on to let long store names wrap.

  • class – your own CSS class.

    [mulopimfwc_store_location_selector title=”Choose your store” use_select2=”on” show_count=”on”]

Shortcodes for the Separate Pro Plugin

  • [mulopimfwc_display_popup] adds a store selection popup or a button that opens it.
  • [mulopimfwc_location_selector] adds a location selector for an individual product.
  • [mulopimfwc_location_info layout="tabs" search="yes"] shows store information with a map, contact details, and hours.
  • [mulopimfwc_location_products] and [mulopimfwc_location_archive] display products and store-specific archive layouts.
  • [mulopimfwc_product_filter location="yes" stock="yes"] adds product filters for location and stock.
  • [mulopimfwc_location_recommendations] shows location-based product recommendations.
  • [mulopimfwc_location_status] shows the store’s Open or Closed status.
sections.faq:
How many locations can I create?

As many as you need. The free plugin has no location limit.

Does each variation get its own stock per location?

Yes. Each variation of a variable product has its own stock and backorder setting at every location.

What happens to the cart when a shopper changes store?

Products the new store cannot supply are removed from the cart, including quantities that are more than the new store has. Products the new store allows on backorder stay.

Can I set different prices per location?

Free uses the normal WooCommerce price at every location. The separate Pro plugin supports regular prices, sale prices, and currencies by location.

Is the free plugin limited in time or by a licence?

No. The free plugin has no licence key and no time limit. All the features on this page keep working.

Does it work with the block checkout and HPOS?

Yes. The order location is saved for both the classic and the block checkout, and order screens work with High-Performance Order Storage.

Where are the settings?

In Location Manage → Settings, in the General, Inventory, Product Visibility, Order & Cart, User Experience, Location Info Management and Advanced tabs.

How do I manage stock across many locations?

Use Location Manage → Stock Central to search products, check stock by store, update stock and backorders, and bulk assign products to locations.

Can shoppers find a nearby location automatically?

Shoppers choose their location in Free. The separate Pro plugin can use browser or IP location tools and display store maps, directions, and business hours.

Can I assign staff to locations?

The separate Pro plugin includes location manager roles and per-location permissions.

Can I import inventory or sync with a POS or ERP?

The separate Pro plugin supports JSON settings, CSV inventory, and ZIP migration workflows. It also provides REST API and webhook integrations for external inventory systems.
sections.changelog:
1.2.7

  • Kept location stock and backorder editing in Stock Central. Free uses the normal WooCommerce price, and existing per-location price data is preserved for the separate Pro plugin.
  • Escaped location names and separators added to product titles.
  • WordPress privacy tools can export or erase saved store locations and activity from earlier versions.
  • Made the optional database index compatible with smaller MySQL index limits and verified it before reporting success.
  • Updated Chart.js and removed the Dashboard’s request-wide PHP limit overrides.

1.2.6

  • Fixed: Changing the store recovers by itself when the page’s security token has expired, and a second change started while the first is still running waits instead of mixing them up.
  • Fixed: The “change notice” setting is respected when it is switched off.
  • Fixed: Customer emails, the thank-you page and My account name the store under each item.
  • Fixed: The plugin pages no longer run wider than a phone screen.
  • Improved: Scripts and styles load as files; every AJAX action carries the plugin prefix; Chart.js and Select2 sit in assets/lib with links to their source code.
  • Improved: Settings tabs sit side by side, as in Pro.
  • Fixed: Administrators and shop managers always reach a product page; a location chosen in their own browser no longer turns other locations’ products into a 404 for them.
  • Fixed: With “Show product page with unavailable message”, the product can no longer be added to the cart at a location that does not sell it.
  • Fixed: The product title names only the shopper’s chosen store, not every store of the product.
  • Fixed: When a store is required, the reason now shows under the disabled Add to cart button.
  • Fixed: Stock Central quick edit saves again when the product has location prices from an earlier Pro installation.
  • Fixed: The product page store choice set to “after title” / “after price” lands there on Astra and OceanWP.
  • Fixed: Location stock fields accept negative stock, an emptied box clears that location’s stock, and bulk removing a location cleans up its stock.
  • Fixed: Admin notices from other plugins show above the plugin header instead of inside it; the Stock Central header and dashboard chart labels no longer run past the edge.
  • Changed: The free plugin’s screens show only what the free plugin does. Settings, fields, sample charts and pages of Pro features are gone; what Pro adds is described on one Get Pro page with a link to the live demo.
  • Changed: The “Upgrade to Pro” settings tab is replaced by the Get Pro page in the plugin menu.
  • Improved: Stock Central has one search box in its header, the same table layout as Pro and stock shown as “14 in stock”.
  • Improved: The Locations screen has one title and one search box, and the Add New Location form scrolls inside its card.
  • Improved: Dropdowns on the plugin screens open as the plugin’s styled list, and the Settings page sits in one framed panel.

1.2.2

  • Fixed: Preserve saved dropdown selections when malformed settings values are submitted, preventing PHP conversion warnings.
  • Improved: Add regression coverage while preserving structured settings and existing Free/Pro feature boundaries.

1.2.1

  • Fixed: Switching locations removes cart items without sufficient stock at the selected location, including variations and quantities spread across multiple cart lines. Allowed backorders are retained.
  • Fixed: Retained cart items save the selected location in cart metadata, sessions and persistent carts.
  • Fixed: Legacy mixed-cart settings from Pro no longer bypass stock validation in the free plugin. Saved settings are preserved.
  • Fixed: Location switching loads saved cart contents before cleanup and keeps the previous selection when the cart or AJAX configuration is unavailable.
  • Fixed: Personal data erasure and user deletion remove matching analytics identifiers from legacy lists and keyed maps while preserving other customers’ data and aggregate totals.
  • Fixed: Product selectors and stock notices handle unavailable WooCommerce functions without fatal errors.

1.2.0

Security
* Added security checks (nonces and permissions) to deleting a saved location, clearing the cart from the location selector, and the deactivation feedback form.
* Location names are shown as plain text in the product editor, so a crafted name can no longer run script.
* Setting descriptions can no longer contain script, iframe, form and similar tags.
* A Location Manager role left behind by an older Pro version loses its administrator capabilities (users keep the role).
* The location tracking endpoint stores nothing while tracking is off.
* Usage data is only sent after “Contribute to Plugincy” is switched on (it is off by default), and the deactivation dialog has a “Skip & Deactivate” button.
* The “Plugin License” tab is now an “Upgrade to Pro” tab: the free plugin no longer activates licences or downloads and installs Pro. Download Pro from your plugincy.com account.

Fixes
* No more critical error (“Call to a member function is_empty() on null”) on store pages and cart checks when another plugin or a cache layer stops WooCommerce from loading the cart.
* “Price at this location” no longer shows $0.00 for variations and shows the price you are actually charged.
* Products added to an existing order in the admin take stock from their location.
* The order’s location follows its items when they all end up at one location after editing.
* The order Location box no longer marks the order’s own location as “Insufficient stock” for units the order already holds.
* Stock Central page 2 no longer repeats the last bulk action or shows “Security check failed”.
* Stock Central bulk action messages are shown again, and Enter in the page number box no longer runs a picked bulk action.
* Location stock is taken once per order line and given back exactly, at the same store, on cancel, failure or refund. Before, stock could drift (double reductions, refunds counted twice).
* Order lines without a location no longer take or restore stock based on the location selected by the admin or by a background task.
* Changing an order line’s or an order’s location on a pending order no longer moves stock (payment takes it at the new store); on on-hold orders the units move from the old store to the new one.
* The order location is saved at checkout, for both the classic and the block checkout, instead of on the thank-you page.
* The “Stock levels reduced” order note shows the real WooCommerce stock change instead of the location stock.
* Location backorder value “no” (from imports) now means no backorders, and with location stock switched off, leftover location stock no longer blocks add to cart.
* Location names in Bengali, Arabic and other non-Latin scripts work with cookies, Stock Central, the order location box and order filters. On the first admin page load after the update, order location values saved in the old form are rewritten once to the form WordPress uses (existing locations only, nothing is deleted).
* “Show grayed out” and “Show with badge” out-of-stock modes now show, and “You may also like” / cross-sells hide other locations’ products as the setting says.
* The selector shortcode no longer empties the whole cart when the location changes: it asks (if that notice is on) and removes only the products the new location doesn’t have. With show_button=”on” the choice is applied by the button. Reloads keep the page’s query string, and two selectors on one page both work.
* A cookie for a deleted or renamed location no longer empties the shop or causes 404 errors.
* The product-page location selector shows in its set position on block themes.
* Saving settings keeps settings the form doesn’t show, so moving to Pro and back no longer loses Pro settings. The title separator keeps its spaces.
* Variation purchase prices save, the Stock Central product column sorts, and removing a product’s last location sticks.
* The legacy orders list shows one location filter instead of two.
* WooCommerce’s stock text and other Select2 fields (such as the checkout country) are no longer restyled, plugin styles no longer change other wp-admin screens, and keyboard focus is visible again.
* Deleting the free plugin while Pro is installed no longer deletes the shared settings.
* Removed PHP warnings on the Stock Central screen.

Performance
* Shop and category pages no longer run one location query per product.

Improvements
* New admin design: a shared header and tabs, and restyled Dashboard, Locations, Stock Central, Location Managers, Analytics and Settings screens.
* Location backorder selects have a new first option, “Use product setting”. Existing products keep their saved value.
* “Settings saved.” message after saving.
* Tools > Export/Erase Personal Data include the customer’s saved store locations.
* Leaflet and Select2 load only where they are used, not on every page.

Compatibility
* Declares compatibility with WooCommerce HPOS and the cart and checkout blocks.
* Guest pages send “Vary: Cookie”, so page caches that honour it keep one copy per location.
* Requires WordPress 5.7 or later. Tested with WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.2.
